# `data/faq.json`

> The FAQ knowledge base for the fictional Georgian operator "ჯიხვი" (Jikhvi): 20 question/answer entries about plans, roaming, SIM cards, payments and branches, stored as JSON.

## What it does and why

This file is data, not code. It holds the facts the assistant may state to customers. Each entry is one FAQ item with an id, a topic, a sample question, the answer text and a keyword string.

The system prompt in `chat.py` currently holds the facts directly (see the decision on the fictional operator). This file is the structured version of those facts, meant for retrieval, so the facts no longer have to sit inside the prompt. Nothing runs it. You read it with `python faq.py` or load it with `json.load`. I can't confirm from the file alone how `faq.py` uses it, so check [faq.py](../faq.py.md).

Quick check that the file is valid JSON and has 20 entries:

```
python -c "import json; print(len(json.load(open('data/faq.json', encoding='utf-8'))))"
```

## How it fits

```
data/faq.json  --read by-->  faq.py  --(answers/facts)-->  chat.py / LLM
```

- It calls nothing. It uses no API, no env vars.
- The Georgian text is UTF-8. Anything that opens it should pass `encoding="utf-8"`, or Windows/WSL defaults may break it.
- The facts (prices, hours, cities) are invented. They belong to a fictional operator.

## Walkthrough

### Lines 1–2, 148–149: the outer list

```json
[
  {
  ...
  }
]
```

- JSON is a text format. `[ ... ]` is an array, which Python loads as a `list`.
- Each `{ ... }` is an object, which Python loads as a `dict`. So the whole file becomes a list of dicts, the same shape as the `history` list in `chat.py`.
- Entries are separated by commas. There is no comma after the last one (line 147). JSON forbids trailing commas, so adding one there would make loading fail.

### Fields shared by every entry

Every entry has exactly five string keys, always in the same order:

- `id`: a short unique English slug such as `plans-overview`. It identifies the entry, so code or logs can say which FAQ item was used.
- `topic`: a short Georgian title for the subject.
- `question`: a typical way a customer would ask it.
- `answer`: the exact text the assistant may say. It is written in 1–2 short sentences, which matches the "1–3 sentences, facts only" prompt rule since the reply is spoken aloud.
- `keywords`: one space-separated string of words and synonyms. It is not a list. It exists so a simple keyword search can match a customer's wording (for example "ესიმ" for "eSIM", or "ლარი" next to "₾"). It also contains Latin tokens like `S`, `GB`, `PIN`.

Quote marks inside answers: the Georgian text uses typographic quotes. It opens with `„` and closes with a plain `"` (for example `„ჯიხვი S"` on line 6). In JSON a plain `"` ends a string. Look at line 6 as written: `„ჯიხვი S\"` is escaped with a backslash, so `\"` is a literal quote character, not the end of the string. That is why `\"` appears everywhere a name or button is quoted.

### Lines 2–29: tariffs (4 entries: `plans-overview`, `plan-s`, `plan-m`, `plan-l`)

- `plans-overview` gives the three monthly plans: S 15 ₾, M 25 ₾, L 40 ₾.
- `plan-s`: 15 ₾, 10 GB, 300 minutes.
- `plan-m`: 25 ₾, 30 GB, unlimited calls inside the Jikhvi network.
- `plan-l`: 40 ₾, unlimited internet and calls.
- `₾` is the lari sign. It is a normal Unicode character in the string.
- Keep these consistent with each other. S, M and L prices appear twice (overview and detail), so a change must be made in both places.

### Lines 30–43: changing plan and extra data (`plan-change`, `extra-data`)

- Change a plan in the app under „ჩემი ტარიფი" → „შეცვლა". It is free and takes effect next month.
- Extra data: 5 GB for 5 ₾, valid to the end of the current month.

### Lines 44–64: roaming and international calls (`roaming-europe`, `roaming-no-package`, `international-calls`)

- Europe roaming package: 20 ₾, 3 GB, 7 days, activated from the app.
- Without a package: 1 ₾ per MB. The answer warns the customer to buy a package first.
- International calls from Georgia: 0.50 ₾/min to Europe, 1 ₾/min elsewhere.
- Note the decimal `0.50` sits inside a string. It is text, not a number.

### Lines 65–85: SIM and eSIM (`esim-activation`, `sim-replace`, `sim-lost`)

- eSIM activation: free, via app „eSIM", scan a QR code.
- Replacing a physical SIM: 5 ₾, in any branch, bring an ID card.
- Lost SIM or phone: block it in the app („უსაფრთხოება" → „SIM-ის დაბლოკვა") or go to a branch with ID. The `→` arrow is plain text.

### Lines 86–106: PIN/PUK and balance (`pin-puk`, `balance-topup`, `balance-check`)

- PUK code is shown in the app („უსაფრთხოება" → „PUK კოდი") or at a branch with ID.
- Top-up: app, card or a quick-payment machine, 0 ₾ commission.
- Balance and remaining GB are on the app's home page. This is the only answer with a single sentence.

### Lines 107–141: numbers, contract and contact (`number-port`, `new-number`, `contract-end`, `branch-hours`, `app-chat`)

- Number porting: free, takes 1–3 working days, via a branch with ID.
- New number: branch with ID, or eSIM in the app. A new SIM is free.
- Ending a contract: only at a branch with ID, free.
- Branches: Monday to Saturday 10:00–19:00, closed Sunday.
- App chat is 24/7 with a human operator. `app-chat` is the entry that backs the "hand off to a human" rule.

### Lines 142–148: coverage (`coverage-5g`)

- 5G in Tbilisi, Batumi and Kutaisi on all plans. 4G elsewhere.

## Trace one run

A customer asks: „რა ღირს როუმინგი ევროპაში?"

1. Some code (not in this file) loads the JSON into a list of 20 dicts.
2. It searches. The words „როუმინგი" and „ევროპაში" match the `question` of entry `roaming-europe` and its keywords `როუმინგი ევროპა`.
3. The entry used is `{"id": "roaming-europe", ..., "answer": "ევროპის როუმინგის პაკეტი ღირს 20 ₾ და მოიცავს 3 GB-ს 7 დღით. ჩაირთვება აპლიკაციიდან."}`.
4. The assistant says that answer. The customer hears the 20 ₾ / 3 GB / 7 days facts.

Note that `roaming-no-package` also mentions roaming. A weak keyword search could pick it instead. Both share `როუმინგი`.

## What can go wrong

- **Invalid JSON.** A missing comma, a trailing comma, or an unescaped `"` inside an answer makes `json.load` raise `json.JSONDecodeError`. Typographic closing quotes must be written `\"`.
- **Wrong encoding.** Opening without `encoding="utf-8"` can produce garbled Georgian on some systems.
- **Inconsistent facts.** Prices live in several entries (S/M/L appear in overview and detail). Nothing checks them against each other or against the prompt in `chat.py`.
- **Weak keyword matching.** `keywords` is a plain string, so matching depends on exact word forms. Georgian is heavily inflected (for example „ევროპაში" vs „ევროპა"), so plain substring or token matching can miss. Synonyms are added by hand only.
- **Overlapping topics.** Several entries share words (`SIM`, `ბარათი`, `როუმინგი`, `ბალანსი`), so a search can return the wrong one.
- **Not covered.** The file has no entries for complaints, billing disputes or personal account data. The assistant cannot look up anything personal. It has to hand off to the app chat (`app-chat`).
- **Invented facts.** All numbers are fictional. Do not present them as a real operator's prices.
